subject: Post-demo: tokenized feature pricing & CAC timeline
messages:
From: kimberly_park
To: Ari Brown <ari.brown@curasense.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@curasense.com>
Cc: aditya_rao, marissa_cole
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: tokenized feature pricing & CAC timeline

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. High-level recap + asks so we can run the unit-econ scenarios you requested.

Summary of agreed inputs (please confirm or correct):
- Primary use-case: in-app summarization and triage for clinical intake forms
- Target launch: Q3 pilot (50k MAUs in pilot region)
- Expected active users for pilot month: 50,000
- Avg events per active user/day: 0.8 (mostly form submits + 1 follow-up prompt)
- Average tokens per event (prompt+response): 1,100 tokens
- Estimated monthly tokens (pilot): ~132M tokens (50k * 0.8 * 1,100 * 30)
- Budget range you mentioned: $6k–$18k / month for inference during pilot (you said the PV team will try for lower but this is the comfortable range)

Requests we heard from your side:
1) Three scenario outputs: conservative / expected / aggressive for $/1M tokens bands + per-feature $ cost for: intake summarization, intent classification, and auto-reply generation.
2) CAC payback examples: provide a 3-feature bundle example with assumed pricing and CAC to show months-to-payback at different adoption rates.
3) Margin targets: you prefer a >50% gross margin target after inference and infra spend. Confirm if that’s a hard constraint.

Next steps from Redwood (proposed):
- I’ll share an updated econ workbook (attached) with scenario tabs and a per-feature breakdown — please review and flag any input changes.
- Aditya (cc’d) will propose a pricing band and recommended contract term that meets your mid-case budget while preserving target margins.
- If the model looks good, we’ll draft an SOW for a Q3 pilot and attach a simple usage SLA.

Attachments: Redwood_Econ_Model_v2.xlsx (scenario tabs), SOW-draft-curasense.pdf (pilot SOW stub)

Would you like us to run a sensitivity table that shows months-to-CAC-payback for payback horizons of 3 / 6 / 12 months? Happy to add that in the next version.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your confirmation on the inputs and the margin threshold.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai

From: Ari Brown <ari.brown@curasense.com>
To: kimberly_park
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@curasense.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: tokenized feature pricing & CAC timeline

Kimberly — thanks, this looks right at a high level. A couple clarifications and one ask: 

Clarifications:
- The 50k MAU figure is for the pilot region only; enterprise-wide rollout could 4x that within 12 months if the pilot metrics hold.
- The budget range I gave ($6k–$18k) was our PM’s comfort band for pilot. The CFO will expect to see a unit-econ that maps to $/feature and payback before we pull legal.

One ask:
Can you provide per-feature examples that assume the following pricing subscription structures?
- $0.5 / MAU / month for basic access + metered inference at $/1M tokens (we want to see combined $ revenue per feature)
- A bundle price where all three features are offered for a single $X/month (show margin and break-even on CAC)

We’d like the sensitivity table (3 / 6 / 12 months payback) as you proposed. Also, please highlight any assumptions about caching or batching that materially change token consumption in production (e.g., prefix caching for recurrent prompts).

Thanks — if you can get an updated workbook by tomorrow morning Pacific we’ll review and set up a follow-up on Friday.

—Ari
Ari Brown
VP Product, CuraSense
ari.brown@curasense.com

From: kimberly_park
To: aditya_rao, marissa_cole
Cc: laura_bennett
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Post-demo: tokenized feature pricing & CAC timeline
Internal — forwarding Ari’s confirmation and asks. Key asks to address in updated workbook:
- Produce 3 scenario tabs (conservative/expected/aggressive) with $/1M token bands that map to per-feature revenue under both (a) MAU + metered inference and (b) single-bundle price.
- Sensitivity: months-to-CAC-payback for 3 / 6 / 12 months. Use realistic CAC for a mid-market buyer: assume CAC = $18k for pilot acquisition (sales + onboarding) unless finance recommends otherwise.
- Show gross margin after inference + infra overhead. Target margin Ari referenced is >50% — propose 55% as a target margin we can defend.

Practical constraints / assumptions to bake in (please call out in a notes cell):
- Apply 20% token reduction in the expected case for caching and client-side truncation.
- Use Redwood fleet cost assumptions: base inference cost = $X per 1M tokens (we’ll put a placeholder and then show target price bands).
- Include a scenario where quantized model variant reduces token cost by 30% (aggressive).

Aditya — can you draft 3 pricing bands (conservative/expected/aggressive) that align to those margin targets? Aim so that the expected band lands inside Ari’s $6k–$18k pilot budget for their expected token volume after caching.
Marissa — can you prepare a one-page breakdown for per-feature $/month (both MAU+metered and bundle) and quick bullets on which features we recommend gating for pilot vs full roll-out (affects CAC and revenue).
Laura — quick sanity check on CAC assumption; if you have a preferred baseline we should use, please update.

I’ve attached the econ workbook (Redwood_Econ_Model_v2.xlsx) and a stub SOW. Planning to send the updated workbook to Ari by 8:00 AM PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: marissa_cole
To: kimberly_park, aditya_rao
Cc: laura_bennett
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: Post-demo: tokenized feature pricing & CAC timeline

Quick numbers for the workbook and the call:

Baseline inputs (expected case) we’ll use for the per-feature calculation:
- Monthly tokens (post-caching): 105.6M (~20% reduction from raw)
- Target $/1M tokens (expected): $2,000
- Per-1M cost to Redwood (fleet + infra estimate placeholder): $500 (we’ll finalize with runtime team)

Per-feature $ (expected case):
- Intake summarization: 1,100 tokens per event -> ~ $2.20 per 1k tokens -> at 1,100 tokens average this maps to $2.20 * 1.1 = $2.42 per event -> scaled monthly = $2.42 * estimated monthly events (50k*0.8*30 = 1.2M events) -> ~$2.9k/month from metered inference portion.
- Intent classification (light): 250 tokens per event -> ~$0.55 per event -> scaled monthly ~$660/month.
- Auto-reply generation (longer): 2,200 tokens per event -> ~$4.84 per event -> scaled monthly assume opt-in for 20% of users -> (50k*0.8*30*0.2 = 240k events) -> ~$1.16M tokens equivalent -> metered revenue ~$2.32k/month.

Bundle example (three features):
- Bundle price (recommended expected): $3.99 / MAU / month + metered credits; for 50k MAU that’s $199.5k list — that’s too big for pilot. Instead, propose pilot bundle: $0.75 / MAU / month + metered at $2k / 1M tokens -> pilot bundle revenue estimate: $37.5k + metered (~$8k) = $45.5k — aligns with CFO scrutiny but above Ari’s mid-range; we’ll show alternative lower trial bundle at $0.25/MAU that lands near $12.5k + metered.

CAC payback (using CAC = $18k):
- At expected margins (55% target) and expected revenue per month ~$45.5k -> gross margin ~$25k/month -> payback ~0.72 months (pilot economics look strong if adoption lands).
- Show sensitivity where adoption is 25% of expected — payback stretches to ~3 months.

Next steps: I’ll add these numbers to the workbook and flag the cells that are placeholders (fleet cost, CAC). We should be able to send to Ari before 08:00 AM PT as requested.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
